mainTopic: Rereading the apparent sins of בני שמואל and דוד, and the dispute between רב and שמואל over whether דוד accepted לשון הרע
overview: This amud continues the statements of רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן that people the פסוקים seem to call sinners did not sin in the simple sense. First, בני שמואל: their 'chasing gain' means they stayed in their own cities instead of traveling to judge like their father, and the תנאים give four different definitions of that 'gain'. Next, דוד: since the שכינה was with him, he did not sin with בת שבע. Each phrase of נתן הנביא's rebuke is reread. 'To do evil' means he only wanted to. He should have tried אוריה in the סנהדרין. בת שבע was already divorced, because every soldier gave his wife a גט before going to war. And אוריה was a מורד במלכות, so his death was not punished. רב sums up that the אוריה matter was דוד's only flaw. אביי קשישא points out that רב also said דוד accepted לשון הרע, and this contradiction remains a קשיא. The גמרא then studies רב's claim from the story of ציבא and מפיבשת, and brings שמואל's view that דוד acted on what he saw himself. שמואל's proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בני שמואל did not truly sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן's statement continues: anyone who says בני שמואל sinned is mistaken. The proof is that the פסוק only says they did not walk in their father's ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Anyone who says that] בני שמואל sinned is simply mistaken. The verse says, 'And it came to pass, when שמואל was old... his sons did not walk in his ways.' This means they did not walk in his ways, but they did not actually sin either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a statement by רבי יונתן, whose opening words appear at the end of the previous עמוד. It claims that בני שמואל were not real sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a careful reading of the wording. The פסוק says 'they did not walk in his ways.' That means they did not reach their father's high level. It does not mean they committed actual sins. Falling short of a great צדיק is different from being a sinner.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a proof פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'אמר רבי שמואל בר נחמני אמר רבי יונתן כל האומר' ('Anyone who says...') are at the end of the previous עמוד (55b).

phrases.english: [Anyone who says] Samuel's sons sinned
phrases.notes: The opening 'Anyone who says' is on the previous page.

phrases.english: is nothing but mistaken,
as it is said: 'And it came to pass, when Samuel was old
and his sons did not walk) in his ways' —
it is in his ways that they did not walk,
but they did not actually sin either.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי שְׁמוּאֵל חָטְאוּ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of 'כל האומר... חטא אינו אלא טועה' statements from 55b.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בני שמואל were not sinners. They only failed to reach their father's level.

steps.title: But the verse says they pursued gain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if they did not sin, how do we explain the words 'ויטו אחרי הבצע' in the same passage?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the verse 'And they turned aside after unjust gain'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem from the very same passage, which clearly seems to describe sin. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק goes on to say they 'turned aside after gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.' That sounds like real sin, which contradicts the claim in step 1. The phrase 'מה אני מקיים' means 'how do I fit this in?' The challenge forces the גמרא to reinterpret those words.

keyTerms.meaning: but then how do I explain/uphold [this verse]?
and they turned aside after unjust gain

phrases.english: But then how do I uphold
'And they turned aside after unjust gain'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 1 using the continuation of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בני שמואל did not sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly describes them chasing gain, which seems to be outright sin.

steps.title: They stayed home instead of traveling to judge
steps.stepSummary: The answer: Samuel traveled from city to city to judge the people. His sons stayed in their own cities so that their attendants and scribes would earn more fees. The פסוק calls this 'chasing gain.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It means they did not act like their father. שמואל הצדיק would travel to all the places of ישראל and judge the people in their own towns, as it says: 'He went year after year and circled בית אל, הגלגל, and המצפה, and judged ישראל.' But his sons did not do this. Instead, they stayed in their own cities in order to increase the fees for their attendants and scribes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains 'chasing gain' as a smaller failing rather than taking bribes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל made himself available by coming to the people. His sons made the people come to them, and this travel brought extra fees to their staff. The פסוק describes this harshly, as if they had chased profit. But it was really a failure to live up to their father's standard, not outright corruption.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יונתן, the 'sin' of בני שמואל was not bribery. It was choosing to stay home and let their staff collect more fees, unlike their father, who traveled to serve the people.

phrases.english: that they did not act like their father,
for Samuel the righteous would travel around
to all the places of Israel
and judge them in their own towns,
as it is said: 'And he went year after year
and circled Beth-El, Gilgal, and Mitzpah
and judged Israel,'
but they did not do so,
rather, they sat in their own cities
in order to increase the fees
for their attendants and their scribes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Chasing gain' means they took bribes and were corrupt.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Chasing gain' means they stayed in their cities, which increased their staff's fees. This was a failure to match their father, not real corruption.

steps.title: תנאים disagree on what their gain was
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this question is already debated by תנאים. Four views are given about what 'ויטו אחרי הבצע' means: asking openly for their portion, pressuring homeowners, forcibly taking an extra basket of מעשר, or forcibly taking only the gifts they were owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of the תנאים. 'And they turned aside after gain': רבי מאיר says they asked for their portions out loud. רבי יהודה says they imposed merchandise on homeowners. רבי עקיבא says they took an extra basket of מעשר by force. רבי יוסי says they took the gifts by force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that earlier תנאים also tried to define exactly what wrong בני שמואל did. They give four different explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא gives the phrase 'chasing gain' a specific, limited meaning. None of them reads it as perverting justice through bribes. רבי עקיבא's view, taking more than they were owed, is the harshest. רבי יוסי's view is the mildest: they took only what was theirs, but they took it by force instead of waiting to be given it. So the range of views parallels the question of how serious their wrong really was.

keyTerms.meaning: this parallels a dispute of the תנאים
they asked for their portion out loud

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume all four תנאים describe the same level of wrongdoing. רבי יוסי says they took only gifts they were actually owed. Their fault was taking them by force rather than waiting to receive them.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of the Tannaim.
'And they turned aside after gain':
Rabbi Meir says:
they asked for their portion out loud.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
they imposed merchandise on homeowners.
Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: קוּפָּה יְתֵירָה שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר נָטְלוּ בִּזְרוֹעַ.
phrases.english: they took an extra basket of tithe by force.
Rabbi Yosei says:
they took the gifts by force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the meaning of 'ויטו אחרי הבצע' discussed in steps 2–3 is already debated among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנאים give four different, limited definitions of the 'gain' that בני שמואל pursued.

steps.title: דוד did not sin
steps.stepSummary: A new statement of רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן: anyone who says דוד sinned is mistaken. The פסוק says that ה׳ was with him in all his ways, and the שכינה cannot rest with someone while he sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Anyone who says דוד sinned is simply mistaken. The verse says, 'And דוד was successful in all his ways, and ה׳ was with him.' Is it possible that sin came to his hand while the שכינה was with him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new statement in the same series, now about דוד המלך and the episode of בת שבע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses a logical argument from the פסוק. If ה׳ was with דוד 'in all his ways,' then the שכינה was always with him. The שכינה would not stay with someone committing a real sin, so דוד did not sin in the simple sense. The גמרא will go on to explain how to read the story of בת שבע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the famous discussion of דוד and בת שבע, which explains how the פסוקים can describe his actions harshly without his being a sinner in the simple sense.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
Anyone who says David sinned
is nothing but mistaken,
as it is said: 'And David was successful in all his ways,
and the Lord was with him, etc.'
Is it possible that sin came to his hand
and the Divine Presence was with him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר דָּוִד חָטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement in the same series of רבי יונתן's statements, moving from בני שמואל to דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד did not sin in the simple sense, because the שכינה was with him in all his ways.

steps.title: How do we explain נתן's rebuke?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that דוד did not sin. It quotes נתן הנביא's rebuke, which says דוד despised the word of ה׳ by doing evil.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if דוד did not sin, how do I explain the פסוק: "Why have you despised the word of ה׳, to do the evil?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem for רבי יונתן's view that דוד did not sin. A פסוק seems to say clearly that he did evil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, רבי יונתן said דוד did not sin. But נתן הנביא's rebuke speaks of 'doing evil,' which sounds like a real sin. The גמרא wants to know how that פסוק fits.

keyTerms.meaning: But how do I explain / uphold (this פסוק)?

phrases.english: But how do I explain
"Why have you despised the word of ה׳
to do the evil"?
phrases.notes: שמואל ב יב:ט, the rebuke of the prophet נתן

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יונתן's statement in Step 5 that דוד did not sin.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן's claim that anyone who says דוד sinned is mistaken.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נתן הנביא says דוד despised ה׳'s word 'to do evil,' which seems to say plainly that he sinned.

steps.title: He wanted to sin but did not
steps.stepSummary: The answer: דוד wanted to do the wrong act but did not actually do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that he wanted to do it, but did not actually do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The 'evil' in the פסוק was only a wish or plan, not an actual sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates wanting to sin from actually sinning. נתן rebuked דוד for what he intended to do, but דוד did not actually carry out the forbidden act the פסוק seems to describe. This keeps רבי יונתן's claim safe. Later steps explain the rest of the rebuke.

phrases.english: That he wanted to do it, but did not do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the פסוק: 'to do evil' means intending, not acting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'to do evil' meant דוד actually committed a sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד only planned or wanted the wrong act. He did not carry it out.

steps.title: רבי proves it from the word 'to do'
steps.stepSummary: רב says that רבי, a descendant of דוד, read the פסוק in דוד's favor. Everywhere else in the תורה, sins are described with 'and he did.' Here it says 'to do,' which shows דוד only wanted to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: רבי, who comes from דוד's family, turns the פסוק around and explains it in דוד's favor. On 'Why have you despised the word of ה׳ to do the evil,' רבי says: this evil is different from every other evil in the תורה. For every other evil in the תורה, it is written 'and he did.' But here it is written 'to do.' That means he wanted to do it but did not do it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב brings support for the answer in Step 7. He quotes רבי, who reads a careful detail in the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי compares this פסוק with all other descriptions of sin in the תורה. Those use 'ויעש' (and he did), a completed act. Here the פסוק says 'לעשות' (to do), which sounds like a plan that was never completed. רב also notes that רבי was a descendant of דוד, which explains why he looked for a reading in דוד's favor.

keyTerms.meaning: Turns over and expounds (searches the פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a single word choice in a פסוק ('לעשות' vs. 'ויעש') can carry a whole interpretation.

phrases.english: Rav said: Rebbi, who descends from David,
turns over and expounds in David's favor.

phrases.aramaic: ״מַדּוּעַ בָּזִיתָ אֶת דְּבַר ה׳ לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרַע״ —
phrases.english: "Why have you despised the word of ה׳ to do the evil":
Rebbi says: This evil is different
from all the evils in the Torah,
for with all the evils in the Torah it is written "and he did,"
but here it is written "to do":
that he wanted to do it, but did not do it.
phrases.notes: The same words as Step 7. Here they are the conclusion of רבי's proof from the wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: רַבִּי דְּאָתֵי מִדָּוִד מְהַפֵּךְ וְדָרֵישׁ בִּזְכוּתֵיהּ דְּדָוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 7 with a proof from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד only intended the evil and did not do it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The unusual word 'לעשות' instead of the usual 'ויעש' used for every other sin in the תורה.

steps.title: אוריה should have been tried in court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains 'you struck אוריה with the sword.' דוד's fault was that he should have judged אוריה in the סנהדרין, and he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You struck אוריה החתי with the sword" means: you should have judged him in the סנהדרין, and you did not judge him that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of נתן's rebuke and explains it so it does not mean murder. The complaint was only about the wrong procedure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אוריה was deserving of death (he rebelled against the king), so killing him was not murder. The problem was that דוד had him killed in battle instead of giving him a proper trial in the סנהדרין. This is still a fault, but a much smaller one than murder.

keyTerms.meaning: אוריה the Hittite, בת שבע's husband

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying it was fine to kill אוריה any way at all. It says אוריה was already guilty, and דוד's mistake was skipping the court process.

phrases.english: "Uriah the Hittite you struck with the sword":
that you should have judged him in the Sanhedrin
and you did not judge him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining נתן's rebuke, phrase by phrase, so it fits the view that דוד did not sin.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the פסוק: the fault was procedure, not murder.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'you struck אוריה' meant דוד murdered an innocent man.
steps.terutzMaskana: אוריה deserved death, but דוד should have tried him in the סנהדרין.

steps.title: בת שבע was permitted to דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains 'you took his wife as your wife.' It means דוד's marriage to her was valid, because she was not really married to אוריה at that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And his wife you took for yourself as a wife" means: you have a valid marriage with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next part of the rebuke. Taking בת שבע was not adultery, because she was able to marry דוד. The next step brings the source for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'you took her as a wife,' and the גמרא reads this as a real, valid marriage. That could only be true if she was free from אוריה. The גמרא now needs to show why she was free, and it does so in Step 11.

phrases.english: "And his wife you took for yourself as a wife":
you have a valid marriage with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next phrase of נתן's rebuke.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the פסוק: the marriage was valid, not adultery.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought דוד took a married woman, which would be adultery.
steps.terutzMaskana: בת שבע could legally marry דוד, so his marriage to her was valid.

steps.title: Soldiers gave their wives a divorce
steps.stepSummary: The source: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן that every soldier in דוד's wars wrote a גט כריתות for his wife. The proof is a פסוק about ישי sending דוד to his brothers at war.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: anyone who goes out to the wars of the house of דוד writes a full divorce document for his wife. As it says: "And these ten cheeses bring to the captain of the thousand, and check on your brothers' welfare, and take their pledge."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves Step 10. בת שבע was already divorced, because every soldier gave his wife a גט before going to war. The פסוק is quoted here, and its explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a soldier went missing in battle with no witnesses, his wife could be stuck, unable to remarry. So soldiers gave a conditional גט, which meant she would count as divorced. That is why בת שבע was free to marry דוד once אוריה died. The proof is the word 'ערבתם' in the פסוק, which the גמרא is about to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Their pledge (understood here as something connected to their wives)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יונתן's view: דוד did not truly sin. 'לעשות' means he only intended. אוריה deserved death but should have had a trial. בת שבע was already divorced, because every soldier gave his wife a גט כריתות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the legal basis for saying דוד did not commit adultery. It also shows a practical rule of conditional divorce for soldiers.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
Anyone who goes out to the war of the house of David
writes a bill of divorce for his wife.
As it says: "And these ten cheeses
bring to the captain of the thousand,
and check on your brothers' welfare,
and take their pledge."
phrases.notes: שמואל א יז:יח. The גמרא explains 'ערבתם' in Steps 12–13.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for Step 10's claim that בת שבע was free to marry דוד.
steps.raayaObject: That בת שבע was not a married woman when דוד took her.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן's rule that soldiers in דוד's wars wrote a גט כריתות, derived from שמואל א יז:יח ('ואת ערבתם תקח').

steps.title: What does the word 'ערובתם' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word 'ערובתם' in the פסוק quoted in the last step.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'ערובתם' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about one word in the פסוק it just quoted about ישי sending דוד to his brothers. It is setting up the next step, which will explain the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof that soldiers wrote a גט only works if 'ערובתם' really refers to a divorce document. So before going further, the גמרא has to define the word.

keyTerms.meaning: Their 'pledge' or 'arrangement'. A word in the פסוק whose meaning is being asked about.

phrases.english: What is 'their arubah'?
phrases.notes: From שמואל א' יז:יח: 'ואת ערובתם תקח'. ישי tells דוד to take the ערובה of his brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a key word in the proof-text quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word 'ערובתם' in the פסוק about ישי and his sons.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it means the things that bind husband and wife
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that 'ערובתם' means the matters shared between a husband and wife. In other words, the marriage bond, which the soldiers' גט would cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: things that are 'mixed together' (shared) between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that 'ערובתם' refers to what connects a man and his wife. So ישי was telling דוד to bring back the גט from his brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ערובה is linked to מעורבים, meaning 'mixed together' or 'shared'. Taking the 'ערובה' means taking the document that settles the marriage bond, which is a גט. This completes the proof that soldiers gave their wives a גט, so בת שבע was not a married woman when דוד took her.

keyTerms.meaning: Between him and her (husband and wife)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
Matters that are shared between him and her.
phrases.notes: Meaning the marriage bond. 'Taking' it means bringing the גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ערובתם' means the matters binding husband and wife, so the פסוק refers to taking a גט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof from step 10 and 11 that בת שבע was not really an אשת איש at the time.

steps.title: Killed 'with the sword of בני עמון': no punishment for אוריה's death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the second half of נתן's rebuke to mean that דוד is not punished for אוריה's death, just as he is not punished for soldiers who fall in battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And him you killed with the sword of בני עמון': just as you are not punished for those killed by the sword of בני עמון, so too you are not punished for אוריה החתי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains another phrase from נתן הנביא's rebuke so that it does not sound like murder. The comparison to the enemy's sword shows that דוד carries no punishment for אוריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king is not punished when soldiers die at the hands of the enemy in war. The פסוק puts אוריה's death in the same group, so it is not counted as murder for which דוד is punished. Step 9 had already said that his fault was only in not judging אוריה in the סנהדרין.

keyTerms.meaning: The sword of the children of עמון, the enemy in that war
Just as ... so too (a comparison formula)

phrases.english: 'And him you have killed with the sword of the children of Ammon':
Just as the sword of the children of Ammon,
you are not punished for it,
so too Uriah the Hittite,
you are not punished for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rebuke פסוק and explains its last phrase, continuing the line of defense started in steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק: the comparison to the enemy's sword lowers דוד's liability.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase sounds like נתן is accusing דוד of murder.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase actually tells us that דוד is not punished for אוריה's death, just like deaths in battle.

steps.title: Why is דוד not punished for אוריה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that דוד carries no punishment for אוריה's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why אוריה's death is not counted against דוד. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison taken from a פסוק still needs a reason in הלכה. Why may a person who is not an enemy soldier be put to death without punishment? The גמרא now looks for that reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the reading in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal reason why אוריה's death does not make דוד punishable.

steps.title: אוריה was a rebel against the king
steps.stepSummary: אוריה was a מורד במלכות, because in front of דוד he called יואב 'my lord'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was a rebel against the kingdom, as he said to דוד: 'And my lord יואב and the servants of my lord are camped in the open field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אוריה rebelled against the king, so he was already deserving of death. The proof is that he called יואב 'my lord' while speaking to דוד himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling someone else 'my lord' in front of the king treats the king's honor lightly. That counts as rebellion against the throne. A מורד במלכות may be put to death, so דוד's mistake was only in how it was done, without a trial, as step 9 explained.

keyTerms.meaning: A rebel against the throne, who may be put to death
'And my lord יואב'. אוריה's words to דוד.

phrases.english: He was a rebel against the throne.
As he said to him:
'And my lord Joab and the servants of my lord'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב' יא:יא. Calling יואב 'my lord' in front of the king.

phrases.english: are camped in the open field.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 and backs up the answer with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אוריה was a מורד במלכות, shown by his calling יואב 'my lord' before the king.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying דוד did nothing wrong at all. Step 9 already said דוד should have judged אוריה in the סנהדרין. Here the point is only that the death itself is not punished as murder.

steps.title: רב: the אוריה matter is דוד's only flaw
steps.stepSummary: רב says that if you examine דוד's life, you find no fault except the matter of אוריה. The proof is a פסוק in מלכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: When you look closely at דוד, you find nothing against him except the matter of אוריה, as it is written: 'only in the matter of אוריה החתי'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a closing summary of דוד's record. He was perfect his whole life except for the אוריה affair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in מלכים א' טו:ה praises דוד for doing right all his days 'except in the matter of אוריה'. This shows that even after all the defenses, the אוריה affair still counts as a real flaw. It is just a much smaller one than the simple reading suggests, and it is the only one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Only in the matter of אוריה'. The proof-text.

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא defends דוד on every point: בת שבע was divorced through the soldiers' גט, and אוריה was a מורד במלכות. Even so, רב concludes that the אוריה affair is the one real stain on דוד's otherwise perfect record.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the balance of the whole sugya. It does not erase דוד's mistake. It limits it.

phrases.english: Rav said:
When you examine David,
you do not find anything in him except for the matter of Uriah,
as it is written:
'Only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כִּי מְעַיְּינַתְּ בֵּיהּ בְּדָוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the defense and admits that the אוריה matter is still a real, though single, flaw.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's only fault in his whole life was the matter of אוריה.

steps.title: רב seems to contradict himself about דוד
steps.stepSummary: אביי קשישא asks how רב could say דוד had no fault except אוריה, when רב also said דוד accepted לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי the Elder pointed out a contradiction between two statements of רב. Did רב really say that? But רב also said: דוד accepted לשון הרע!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי קשישא sets one statement of רב against another statement of רב and shows that they clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17 רב said דוד's only flaw was the matter of אוריה. But accepting לשון הרע is also a sin. So if רב himself says דוד did this, דוד had a second fault, and the first statement looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He 'throws' one source against another, meaning he points out a contradiction
One statement of רב against another statement of רב
Negative talk about another person. Believing it is also forbidden.
אביי the Elder, an earlier sage. He is not the famous אביי.

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the famous אביי, the student of רבה. 'קשישא' means 'the Elder', a different, earlier sage.

phrases.english: Abaye the Elder contrasted a statement of Rav with another of Rav:
Did Rav really say this?
But didn't Rav say:
David accepted lashon hara.
phrases.notes: Accepting slander is itself forbidden, so this would be another fault.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי קַשִּׁישָׁא רָמֵי דְּרַב אַדְּרַב: מִי אָמַר רַב הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement in Step 17 that אוריה was דוד's only fault.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that דוד had no fault except אוריה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב elsewhere says דוד accepted לשון הרע, which is a second fault.

steps.title: The contradiction stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the question with 'קשיא'. The difficulty remains and no answer is given.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to the contradiction, and it moves on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' means the question stands but does not cancel the statement. Both statements of רב remain on record, with an open difficulty between them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is difficult.' The question is left without an answer.

steps.whatToRemember: רב's two statements about דוד (only אוריה / accepted לשון הרע) are left in tension. The גמרא does not resolve it.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes Step 18's challenge without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction in רב's statements remains unresolved.

steps.title: רב's statement and proof that ציבא first lied about מפיבשת
steps.stepSummary: Looking at the statement itself, רב says דוד accepted לשון הרע. He first shows from two פסוקים that ציבא had already lied about מפיבשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: רב said דוד accepted לשון הרע. As it is written: 'The king said to him: Where is he? ציבא said to the king: He is in the house of מכיר בן עמיאל, in לא דבר.' And it is written: 'King דוד sent and took him from the house of מכיר בן עמיאל, from לא דבר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now studies רב's second statement on its own. רב begins his proof by showing that ציבא lied about מפיבשת the first time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ציבא said מפיבשת was 'בלא דבר', meaning empty of Torah. When דוד brought him, the פסוק says 'מלא דבר', read as 'full of Torah'. So דוד saw for himself that ציבא's report was false. This sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself'. We now study a statement that was quoted earlier in passing.
Place name 'Lo-Devar', read as 'without a word (of Torah)'

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא דבר' is really a place name. The דרשה plays on the difference between 'בלא' (without) and 'מלא' (full).

phrases.english: The matter itself.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: קִיבֵּל דָּוִד לָשׁוֹן הָרָע,
phrases.english: Rav said: David accepted lashon hara,
as it is written: 'And the king said to him: Where is he?'
And Ziba said to the king:

phrases.aramaic: הִנֵּה הוּא בֵּית מָכִיר בֶּן עַמִּיאֵל
phrases.english: Behold, he is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel,
in Lo-Devar (without Torah).'
And it is written: 'The king sent and took him'
from the house of Machir son of Ammiel,
from Lo-Devar (full of Torah).'
phrases.notes: דוד found him full of תורה, which shows ציבא lied.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. רַב אָמַר: קִיבֵּל דָּוִד לָשׁוֹן הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to examine on its own the statement of רב quoted in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד accepted לשון הרע. The first stage of the proof is that ציבא was already shown to be a liar.

steps.title: ציבא slanders מפיבשת a second time
steps.stepSummary: Once דוד knew ציבא was a liar, why did he believe him when ציבא spoke against מפיבשת again? The פסוק shows the second slander: ציבא said מפיבשת stayed in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, after דוד saw that ציבא was a liar, when ציבא slandered מפיבשת again, why did דוד accept it from him? As it is written: 'The king said to ציבא: Where is your master's son? ציבא said to the king: Behold, he is staying in ירושלים, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב continues his proof. He asks rhetorically why דוד trusted a known liar, and quotes the second slander.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the core of רב's argument. דוד had already caught ציבא lying, so believing his new report about מפיבשת cannot be excused. That is exactly what accepting לשון הרע means.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now, since...' It introduces a logical point.

phrases.english: Now, since he saw that he was a liar,
when he again slandered him,
why did he accept it from him?
As it is written: 'And the king said to Ziba:'
Where is your master's son?
And Ziba said to the king:
Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem, etc.'
phrases.notes: ציבא claims מפיבשת hoped to regain the kingdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 20: since ציבא was already shown to be a liar, believing him again was wrong.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד's acceptance of ציבא's report was improper לשון הרע

steps.title: How do we know דוד believed ציבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that דוד actually accepted ציבא's second report.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he accepted it from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof that דוד really believed the report. Hearing it alone is not enough. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing slander is not the same as acting on it. For רב's claim to hold, we need evidence that דוד believed it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And from where do we know?' A request for a source.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he accepted it from him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for evidence that the slander in Step 21 was actually believed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that דוד acted on ציבא's report

steps.title: דוד gives מפיבשת's property to ציבא
steps.stepSummary: דוד tells ציבא that everything belonging to מפיבשת is now his, which shows that he believed the slander.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'The king said: Behold, all that belongs to מפיבשת is yours. And ציבא said: I bow down; may I find favor in the eyes of the king.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק: דוד transferred מפיבשת's property to ציבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving away מפיבשת's property is a concrete action. It proves דוד believed ציבא, and this completes רב's proof.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's full proof: ציבא lied once ('בלא דבר' vs. 'מלא דבר'), slandered מפיבשת again, and דוד still gave him מפיבשת's property.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the king said:'
Behold, yours is all that belongs to Mephibosheth.
And Ziba said: I bow down;
may I find favor in the eyes of the king.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ הִנֵּה לְךָ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר לִמְפִיבוֹשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22's request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דוד gave מפיבשת's property to ציבא (שמואל ב טז:ד), so he believed the slander.

steps.title: שמואל: דוד saw evidence himself
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. דוד did not accept לשון הרע; he saw clear signs in מפיבשת that seemed to confirm the report.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: דוד did not accept לשון הרע. He saw evident signs in him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposing view. דוד based his judgment on what he saw himself, not on ציבא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Acting on visible evidence is not accepting לשון הרע. According to שמואל, דוד's decision came from his own observation, so it was not a sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a principle: acting on clear evidence that you see yourself is different from believing slander that someone tells you.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
David did not accept lashon hara;
he saw evident signs in him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: לֹא קִיבֵּל דָּוִד לָשׁוֹן הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רב's view (Steps 20–23).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד acted on visible evidence, not on לשון הרע.

steps.title: מפיבשת's neglected appearance and his explanation
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's proof: מפיבשת came to דוד unkempt, which looked like mourning over דוד's safe return. The next פסוק begins מפיבשת's explanation that his servant tricked him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'מפיבשת בן שאול came down to meet the king, and he had not tended his feet, nor trimmed his mustache, nor washed his clothes, etc.' And it is written: 'When he came to ירושלים to meet the king, the king said to him: Why did you not go with me, מפיבשת? He said: My lord the king, my servant deceived me, for your servant said: I will saddle the donkey, ride on it, and go with the king, for lame is...'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל brings פסוקים to show what דוד saw. This passage ends in the middle of the second פסוק, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says מפיבשת neglected himself 'from the day the king left until the day he returned in peace'. To דוד this looked like sadness that he came back safely, which matched ציבא's charge. The second פסוק opens מפיבשת's defense that ציבא tricked him.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not tend to his feet

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וּמְפִיבוֹשֶׁת בֶּן שָׁאוּל יָרַד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ
phrases.english: As it is written: 'And Mephibosheth son of Saul came down to meet the king,'
and he had not tended his feet,
nor trimmed his mustache,
nor washed his clothes, etc.'
phrases.notes: The rest of the verse, 'until the day he came in peace', made it look like mourning over דוד's safe return.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי כִּי בָא יְרוּשָׁלִַים לִקְרַאת הַמֶּלֶךְ
phrases.english: And it is written: 'And when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king,'
the king said to him:
Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?
He said: My lord the king, my servant deceived me,
for your servant said:
I will saddle the donkey for myself and ride on it
and go with the king, for lame is...
phrases.notes: The verse continues on the next amud: '...your servant'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וּמְפִיבוֹשֶׁת בֶּן שָׁאוּל יָרַד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוקים behind שמואל's claim in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד saw visible signs suggesting מפיבשת was disloyal
